chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Safarjala al-Kufi said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran said: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Mansur said: He narrated to us Harb ibn al-Husayn from Ibrahim al-Shaybani from Abu al-Jarud said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'A day and a bit.' He said to him: 'If we were like you are, we would have taken it as a Hijra (migration/exile).'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the distance to the grave of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) uses the hypothetical migration (Hijrah) to the grave of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to emphasize the spiritual centrality of the Imams' resting places. The reference to 'Hijrah' alludes to the early Islamic practice of relocating for religious authority, suggesting that proximity to the Imam’s grave fosters a deeper connection to divine guidance and serves as a focal point for the community's spiritual life.
